title: Graceful eviction and rollback protocol for hot canaries with session-aware drain
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a session-aware eviction and automated rollback protocol for high-pressure (hot) canaries. Backwards-compatible opt-in rollout policy annotation; observability and test harness updates included.
description:
Motivation: In production canary rollouts we observed intermittent customer session disruption when a small percentage of traffic (hot canaries) experienced rapid capacity pressure or degraded resource signals. Existing rollback gates detected regressions but could still cause abrupt user-facing session resets because instances were evicted immediately. This PR implements a graceful eviction and automated rollback protocol that prioritizes session continuity while still enabling fast mitigation of bad model variants.

What this PR changes (high level): implements a session-aware drain path in the serving runtime, adds an eviction window and token-count based drain threshold, introduces a canary health probe that feeds the rollout controller, and extends the controller with a multi-metric rollback policy (latency P95, error-rate, cost-per-token anomaly). The protocol performs snapshot captures for replay on rollback and records per-session affinity so in-flight sessions can complete or be redirected to a fallback variant.

Key behaviors: 1) Opt-in by rollout annotation: rollouts that set rollout.k8s.redwood.io/hot-canary-eviction: "true" enable the protocol. 2) Graceful drain: instances marked for eviction enter a drain window (configurable, default 30s) and will only evict when remaining active token count < drain_threshold (default 1024 tokens) or time window expires. 3) Session-aware routing: session-affined requests are preferentially routed to the same model variant for the duration of the session; when eviction must proceed, the runtime attempts handoff to a compatible variant rather than immediate termination. 4) Multi-signal rollback: controller evaluates rolling window metrics and can trigger automatic rollback if configured gates breach for X consecutive windows. 5) Snapshot + replay: on automatic rollback, the controller archives a compact snapshot of recent requests for postmortem replay in the eval harness.

Implementation notes: runtime: added eviction hook in router and KV cache draining logic (runtime/eviction.go, runtime/session_affinity.go). controller: extended rollout API and controller state machine (controller/rollout/eviction_policy.go), added health probe aggregator (controller/telemetry/aggregate_probe.go). CLI/annotations: rollout annotations and defaults in docs and schema (api/v1/rollout_types.go). Observability: new metrics exported (rollout_eviction_start, rollout_eviction_complete, drain_token_count, canary_snapshot_size) plus tracing spans. Tests: unit tests for drain math and session routing, integration e2e harness that simulates hot traffic patterns and validates no session resets during graceful drains, chaos test target that simulates node OOM during canary.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: the feature is disabled by default and opt-in via rollout annotation. Existing rollouts are unaffected. The controller exposes feature flags for gradual enablement in Dedicated and Private deployments.

Commit summary: see commits below for incremental changes. CI: initial CI run had a flaky e2e (timing) which was addressed by making the drain window deterministic in the test; final CI run passed.

Related work and tickets: ENG-4821 (flow-level eviction model), ENG-4890 (rollback multi-signal gates), SUP-1002 (customer incident that motivated emergency patch).

Checklist: [x] design doc review completed, [x] unit tests added, [x] e2e harness updated, [x] metrics/tracing wired, [x] docs/annotation examples added, [x] canary in staging observed for 48h, [x] release notes drafted.

Merge notes: squash-merged after approvals; migration is configuration-only. Rollout to production will start behind a feature flag and with a 72-hour monitoring window.

review_comments: Marco Chen (review): Can you clarify how session affinity affects cache reuse? The runtime change looks good but we need to avoid catastrophic cache fragmentation.

Aisha Patel (reply): The session affinity token is shallow and not used as a cache key by default. We added a fast-path that maps sessions to the same KV namespace to preserve cache locality; see runtime/session_affinity.go comments and unit tests.
Lena Müller (request changes): Increase observability on token-count decay calculation. I want a metric that samples pre/post drain token distribution.
